Isaac Companion
Features Source Download

macOS & Windows · Afterbirth+ · no mod required

Know what you just picked up.

Isaac never tells you what your stats actually are. This reads the game's own log while you play, works out your real damage and fire rate, and warns you when an item you just took is doing nothing at all.

Your build, while you're in it

Every number is computed from your actual run — base stat, what the items did, and the total. Damage runs through a square-root curve, so "+0.3 Damage" is almost never worth +0.3.

Why bother

Four things no wiki and no in-game mod can do, because none of them know what you are already carrying.

Dead items

Knows when a pickup is wasted

Take Technology while holding Brimstone and the laser never fires. The app reads Afterbirth+'s real precedence ladder and says so, instead of leaving you to wonder.

Real numbers

Your stats, not the wiki's

Base + change = total, on every stat, reconciling on screen. Clamps and multipliers included; anything the game doesn't document is marked estimated rather than guessed.

Zero input

Tracks itself

It tails the log Isaac already writes. Nothing is injected, no mod is enabled — so your Steam achievements keep counting.

Re-rolls

Worth the D6?

Scores the pedestal against everything still in that pool, weighted properly, using your current build — and refuses to answer for items a stat score can't represent.

Everything in it

Four things, and they all run off one log file the game already writes.

Overlay

What that item just did

A borderless always-on-top panel over the fullscreen game. It does not just show your stats — it shows the change your last pickup made, per stat, held until the next one. Ipecac reads +21.00 damage and −2.55 tears, with the item's name underneath.

Overlay

Built how you want it

Around 35 settings in their own tab, with a live mini-screen of your actual display: drag the miniature to move the real window, click a part to take it off. Click-through, corner snapping, per-display placement, opacity, text scale, compact mode, accent stat. It appears when Isaac launches and gets out of the way when you quit.

Browser

775 items, by description

Every item, card, pill and trinket — searchable by name, by effect, or by colour measured off the sprite itself, so "grey" or "gold" finds the one you half-remember. 359 enemies with HP, 403 achievements with their unlock conditions and full-size art.

Browser

Sprites that move

Enemy icons play the idle loop from their own animation files, pills cycle every colour the game deals, and an item with a real baked-in effect gets a backdrop drawn for that effect — poison creeps, fire licks up from the floor, brimstone sweeps across. Off-screen rows stop animating entirely.

Run

Pills and cards, read off the screen

The log says a pocket item was used but never which one — and by then the slot is empty. So the slot is read beforehand and the use is attributed to it. A card is named outright; a pill is harder, because the game reshuffles which colour does what every run, so you say what one did once and every later pill of that colour counts itself. Ones taken before you named the colour are backfilled.

Run

Numbers checked against the game

Turn on the comparison table, type what the HUD shows, and any disagreement is a bug in the stat model rather than in your reading of it. It found three of Cain's six base stats wrong. At the start of a run the HUD is the character's baseline, so those numbers can be saved as measured base stats — play a character once and its row is settled from the game itself, not from a wiki.

Advisor

Worth taking?

In a Devil, Treasure or Angel room it reads the pedestals off the screen — passively, no injection — and scores what is on them against your build and what is left in that pool. It refuses to answer where a stat score cannot represent the item.

Windows

The same engine

A single 440 KB executable with no installer and no runtime. It runs the same log parser and the same stat model, tested against the same fixtures, and serves the readout in your browser. The overlay and the pedestal scanner are macOS window-server features, so they are absent rather than faked.

Open source

Every line of it is on GitHub under the MIT licence — the Swift app, the Windows build, the data pipeline and the page you are reading. The stat model is the part worth reading: it is commented with why each number is what it is, and which ones nobody can settle.

Not in the repo

Nobody else's work

The item descriptions come from the External Item Descriptions mod, which ships without a licence — so that snapshot is not redistributed. It is generated from your own install at build time, along with every sprite and every item name, which come out of your own copy of the game.

Verified, not asserted

Both engines agree

The Windows stat engine is tested against the same fixtures as the macOS one — Ipecac is exactly 24.50, Sad Onion floors to 3.75/s. If the two builds ever disagree about a number, the test fails instead of your screen being quietly wrong.

A fan tool

Not affiliated

The Binding of Isaac is Nicalis and Edmund McMillen's. This reads a log file the game already writes and never touches the game, which is the whole reason your achievements keep counting.

Get it

One build, every Mac: the binary is universal — arm64 and x86_64 in the same file — so an M-series Mac and a 2017 Intel MacBook run the same download natively, with no Rosetta and nothing to choose between. There is a Windows build too, further down.

Other formats
1

Drag it to Applications

The disk image opens with an Applications shortcut beside it.

2

Right-click the app and choose Open

Then click Open in the dialog. Just this once — every launch after that is a normal double-click.

macOS asks because the app is signed with a self-signed certificate rather than a paid Apple Developer ID. It is the same dialog any small independent app gets. Nothing about the app differs either way, and the disk image repeats these steps so you don't have to remember them.

1

Put the .exe wherever you like

There is no installer and nothing to set up — it is one file. It writes only beside itself and never touches your game.

2

If Windows says “Windows protected your PC”

Click More info, then Run anyway. Just this once.

SmartScreen shows that for any program it has not seen downloaded many times before, which a new independent release never has. It is not a virus warning. The checksum of every file is published beside it on the releases page if you want to verify the download yourself.

3

It opens in your browser

The window that appears is the app. Leave it running while you play; it reads the log the game already writes and updates itself as you go.

1

Make it executable and run it

One binary, no installer and no packages to add.

chmod +x IsaacCompanion-linux-x64 && ./IsaacCompanion-linux-x64

2

It opens in your browser

The window that appears is the app. Leave it running while you play — it reads the log the game already writes, from ~/.local/share/binding of isaac afterbirth+/, and updates itself as you go.

Proton and native builds both write there. The overlay and the pedestal scanner are macOS window-server features, so they are absent rather than faked.

Prefer a terminal? One command does the same thing.
$ xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/IsaacCompanion.app
$ open /Applications/IsaacCompanion.app
On first launch

It finds your game

Reads Steam's own manifest to see which release you own — Rebirth, Afterbirth, Afterbirth+, Repentance or Repentance+ — and picks the matching log file, description set and data expectations.

Verified on

Afterbirth+

Every number in the app is checked against Afterbirth+ values. Other releases are detected and wired up, but their item and pool tables live inside game archives, so they are only built once you own that release.

Needs

macOS or Windows

Item data is extracted from your own install, once, on first run. Nothing is downloaded and no mod is enabled, so achievements keep counting. The Mac build is universal — Apple Silicon and Intel in one binary; the Windows build is a single executable.

Item data derived from your own Afterbirth+ install and the External Item Descriptions project. Colours are measured from the game's sprites. Not affiliated with Nicalis or Edmund McMillen.

Settings

Motion and effects are two separate switches — turn either one off and the other keeps working. Your choice is remembered in this browser.

Your system is set to reduce motion, so both switches start off. You can still turn either one on.

Entry animations

The slide-and-fade a row makes as it scrolls into view. Off means rows simply appear in place.

Effect overlays

The poison, fire, and blood wash that plays across a row and fades. Off means rows stay plain.

Minimalist effects

On, only things that really do it in-game move — Ipecac drips, Brimstone burns, and everything else sits perfectly still. Off, plain items borrow a stand-in effect so the whole list has some life to it.

Animated backgrounds

When you open an item that has a real effect, that effect drifts behind its card. Off keeps the same backdrop, it just holds still instead of moving.
